title.zh: 卷九十六 志第七十二 藝文一
title.raw: 卷九十六 志第七十二 藝文一 Volume 96 Treatises 72: Arts and Literature 1

sentences.zh: 明太祖定元都，大將軍收圖籍致之南京，復詔求四方遺書，設祕書監丞，尋改翰林典籍以掌之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Ming pacified the Yuan capital, the great general collected maps and registers and sent them to Nanjing; he also issued an edict seeking lost books from all quarters, established the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat Directorate, and soon changed it to Hanlin keeper of records to manage them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongwu Emperor secured the Yuan capital, his generals gathered maps and archives and conveyed them to Nanjing. He then ordered a search for lost books throughout the realm, appointed a vice director of the Secretariat Directorate to oversee them, and shortly afterward reassigned the duty to Hanlin keepers of the archives.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，帝御便殿閱書史，問文淵閣藏書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle, the emperor attended the informal hall to read histories and asked about the books stored in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yongle reign, the emperor withdrew to the informal hall to read histories and inquired how many books were held in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

translations.literal: Xie Jin replied that there were still many gaps and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jin answered that the collection was still full of gaps and omissions.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「土庶家稍有餘資，尚欲積書，況朝廷乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When common families have even a little surplus, they still wish to accumulate books—how much more should the court?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even humble households with a little spare means still want to build up libraries—how much more ought the throne to do so?

sentences.zh: 遂命禮部尚書鄭賜遣使訪購，惟其所欲與之，勿較值。

translations.literal: He then ordered Minister of Rites Zheng Ci to send envoys to seek and purchase books, giving whatever the owners desired and not haggling over price.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Zheng Ci, the Minister of Rites, to send agents to seek out and buy books, paying whatever sellers asked without bargaining over price.

sentences.zh: 北京既建，詔修撰陳循取文淵閣書一部至百部，各擇其一，得百櫃，運致北京。

translations.literal: After Beijing was established as capital, an edict ordered Compiler Chen Xun to take from one to one hundred copies of each work in the Wenyuan Pavilion collection, choosing one of each, obtaining one hundred cabinets, and transporting them to Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Beijing had been made the capital, the court ordered the compiler Chen Xun to draw from the Wenyuan holdings: for every title held in one to one hundred copies, he was to choose a single exemplar. In this way he filled one hundred cabinets and had them shipped to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗臨視文淵閣，親披閱經史，與少傅楊士奇等討論，因賜士奇等詩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once personally inspected the Wenyuan Pavilion, unrolled and read the classics and histories himself, discussed them with Junior Tutor Yang Shiqi and others, and thereupon bestowed poems on Shiqi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor once visited the Wenyuan Pavilion in person, opened the classics and histories himself, and debated them with Yang Shiqi and other grand secretaries, for which he rewarded them with poems of his own composition.

sentences.zh: 是時，祕閣貯書約二萬餘部，近百萬卷，刻本十三，抄本十七。

translations.literal: At that time the secret repository held about twenty thousand titles, nearly a million scrolls; printed editions and manuscript copies stood in a ratio of thirteen to seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial library held roughly twenty thousand titles and nearly a million scrolls, with printed editions and manuscript copies in a proportion of about thirteen to seventeen.

sentences.zh: 正統間，士奇等言：「文淵閣所貯書籍，有祖宗御製文集及古今經史子集之書，向貯左順門北廊，今移於文淵閣、東閣，臣等逐一點勘，編成書目，請用寶鈐識，永久臧。」

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, Shiqi and others said: "The books stored in the Wenyuan Pavilion include the collected writings in the imperial hand of our ancestors as well as works of the classics, histories, masters, and belles-lettres from ancient and modern times. They were formerly kept in the north corridor of the Left Shun Gate and have now been moved to the Wenyuan and Eastern Pavilions. We have checked them item by item, compiled a catalogue, and ask that an imperial seal be applied for permanent safekeeping."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign Yang Shiqi and his colleagues reported: "The Wenyuan collection includes our forebears' imperial writings and the full range of classical, historical, philosophical, and literary works from every age. Formerly shelved in the north corridor of the Left Shun Gate, these volumes have now been moved to the Wenyuan and Eastern Pavilions. We have inventoried them one by one and drawn up a catalogue; we ask that the imperial seal be affixed so they may be preserved in perpetuity.

translations.literal: An imperial rescript said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied, "Let it be so."

sentences.zh: 正德十年，大學士樑儲等請檢內閣並東閣藏書殘闕者，令原管主事李繼先等次第修補。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengde, Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others requested that damaged and missing volumes among the books stored in the Grand Secretariat and Eastern Pavilion be inspected, and that Li Jixian and other supervising secretaries in charge be ordered to repair them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhengde reign Grand Secretary Liang Chu and his colleagues asked that incomplete or damaged volumes in the Grand Secretariat and Eastern Pavilion collections be surveyed, and that Li Jixian and the other supervising secretaries who had long managed the holdings be directed to restore them in turn.

sentences.zh: 先是，祕閣書籍皆宋、元所遺，無不精美，裝用倒摺，四周外向，蟲鼠不能損。

translations.literal: Earlier, the books in the secret repository were all legacies of the Song and Yuan, without exception fine; they were bound with folded-back covers turned outward on all four sides so that insects and rodents could not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the palace library's holdings were almost entirely fine Song and Yuan survivals, bound with their folded covers turned outward on every side so that worms and rats could not reach the pages.

sentences.zh: 迄流賊之亂，宋刻元鐫胥歸殘闕。

translations.literal: By the time of the turmoil of the roving bandits, Song imprints and Yuan engravings alike had become damaged and incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: By the disorders of the rebel armies, Song block-prints and Yuan editions alike had been reduced to tattered remnants.

sentences.zh: 至明御製詩文，內府鏤板，而儒臣奉敕修纂之書及象魏佈告之訓，卷帙既夥，文藻復優，當時頒行天下。

translations.literal: As for the Ming dynasty's imperially composed poetry and prose, engraved on blocks in the inner palace, together with books compiled by Confucian officials by imperial command and the instructions promulgated at the Gate of Audience, the number of scrolls was already great and the literary polish moreover excellent; at the time they were issued throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ming imperial poetry and prose were cut on palace blocks; works that scholar-officials compiled by edict and proclamations posted at the Gate of Audience were likewise voluminous and finely wrought, and in their day were distributed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 外此則名公卿之論撰，騷人墨客一家之言，其工者深醇大雅，卓卓可傳。

translations.literal: Beyond these were the treatises of eminent ministers and the individual voices of poets and men of letters; the accomplished among them were deep, pure, and broadly elegant, outstanding and fit to be handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the court corpus stood the writings of celebrated statesmen and the private voices of poets and scholars; the best of these were grave, refined, and broadly elegant—works plainly worthy of transmission.

sentences.zh: 即有怪奇駁雜出乎其間，亦足以考風氣之正變，辨古學之源流，識大識小，掌故備焉。

translations.literal: Even when strange, curious, or heterogeneous works appeared among them, they were still sufficient to examine the orthodox and the aberrant in literary fashion, distinguish the sources and currents of ancient learning, discern the great and the small, and furnish abundant historical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Even the odd and heterogeneous pieces that appeared among them suffice to trace shifts in literary taste, map the currents of classical learning, and gather precedent great and small.

sentences.zh: 挹其華實，無讓前徽，可不謂文運之盛歟！

translations.literal: Savoring their blossom and fruit, they yield nothing to the glories of earlier ages—can this fail to be called the flourishing of the literary fortune?
translations.idiomatic: In flower and fruit together they yield nothing to earlier ages—can one deny that the literary age had reached its height!

sentences.zh: 四部之目，昉自荀勖，晉、宋以來因之。

translations.literal: The fourfold classification had its beginning with Xun Xu; from Jin and Song onward it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The fourfold bibliographic division originated with Xun Xu and was followed from the Jin and Song dynasties onward.

sentences.zh: 前史兼錄古今載籍，以為皆其時柱下之所有也。

translations.literal: Earlier histories recorded together writings ancient and modern, taking them all to be what was held by the Keeper of Archives of that time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynastic histories listed writings both ancient and modern on the assumption that all were held in the archives of their own day.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆中，修撰焦竑修國史，輯《經籍志》，號稱詳博。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign of Ming, Compiler Jiao Hong revised the dynastic history and compiled the "Treatise on Classics and Writings," which was acclaimed as detailed and comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign the compiler Jiao Hong worked on the dynastic history and compiled a Treatise on Classics and Writings that was praised as exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 然延閣廣內之藏，竑亦無從遍覽，則前代陳編，何憑記錄，區區掇拾遺聞，冀以上承《隋志》，而贗書錯列，徒滋訛舛。

translations.literal: Yet the collections of the Extended Pavilion and the Broad Inner Quarters Hong likewise had no means to survey in full; then upon what could records of the piled-up writings of former dynasties rely? Merely gathering stray reports in hope of continuing the Sui Treatise, while forged books were wrongly entered—only multiplying errors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even Hong could not survey the full holdings of the imperial libraries; on what basis, then, could he record the accumulated writings of earlier ages? He could only patch together hearsay in hope of continuing the Sui catalogue, while spurious works were misfiled and errors multiplied.

sentences.zh: 故今第就二百七十年各家著述，稍為釐次，勒成一志。

translations.literal: Therefore the present account takes only the writings of various authors over the two hundred and seventy years, arranges them somewhat in order, and compiles them into one treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The present treatise therefore limits itself to works produced over the dynasty's two hundred and seventy years, sets them in rough order, and compiles them into a single catalogue.

sentences.zh: 凡卷數莫考、疑信未定者，甯闕而不詳云。

translations.literal: Whenever the number of scrolls cannot be verified or authenticity remains uncertain, it is better to omit than to elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: Where scroll counts cannot be verified or authenticity remains doubtful, entries are omitted rather than filled in speculatively.

sentences.zh: 經類十：一曰《易》類，二曰《書》類，三曰《詩》類，四曰《禮》類，五曰《樂》類，六曰《春秋》類，七曰《孝經》類，八曰諸經類，九曰《四書》類，十曰小學類。

translations.literal: The Classics comprise ten categories: first, Changes; second, Documents; third, Odes; fourth, Rites; fifth, Music; sixth, Spring and Autumn; seventh, Filial Piety; eighth, miscellaneous classics; ninth, Four Books; tenth, elementary learning.
translations.idiomatic: The Classics fall into ten categories: (1) the Book of Changes, (2) the Book of Documents, (3) the Book of Odes, (4) the Rites, (5) Music, (6) the Spring and Autumn Annals, (7) the Classic of Filial Piety, (8) miscellaneous classics, (9) the Four Books, and (10) philology and elementary learning.
